rules: Every record remains a candidate until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin, or diffusion.
Publication and index dates are preserved separately; indexing novelty is not publication novelty.
Preprints are not peer-reviewed evidence and remain separately labeled.
Human remains, ancient DNA, and mortuary contexts require cultural-sensitivity review before public presentation.
Biomedical mechanism is not evidence of historical religious meaning or diagnosis.

new_candidates.title: Ancient DNA Reveals Limited Hunter-Gatherer Ancestry in the Cerny Culture (Middle Neolithic, France) Despite Hunting-Associated Practices
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Genome-wide data from 28 individuals indicate that distinctive Cerny hunting-associated funerary traits were not accompanied by unusually high Mesolithic hunter-gatherer ancestry, directly pressuring ancestry-to-cultural-practice inference.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Distinctive material or funerary practices do not by themselves identify ancestry, descent, migration, or the beliefs that motivated those practices.

provenance.source: American Journal of Biological Anthropology / Wiley

new_candidates.title: Investigating ancient human DNA preservation on cave walls and in rock art
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Ancient human DNA was recovered from cave-wall contexts, including one pigmented sample, showing that wall surfaces can preserve human biological traces and may eventually help connect cave use to populations.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The authors explicitly do not establish that recovered DNA belongs to the maker of the art; pigment and DNA deposition may be separated by long periods and unpigmented surfaces can also contain human DNA.

new_candidates.title: A signaling signature distinguishes hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic psychedelics
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: The study reports a distinct intracellular phosphorylation signature separating hallucinogenic serotonergic compounds from related non-hallucinogenic compounds under defined experimental conditions, offering a mechanistic layer for altered-state research.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: In-vitro signaling is not equivalent to subjective mystical experience, religious interpretation, ritual function, or historical entheogen use.

provenance.version_note: early peer-reviewed citable version, subject to later copyediting

new_candidates.title: What’s the point? Variation and innovation of Neolithic arrowhead technology in northwest Arabia
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Attribute analysis reports both similarities with Levantine arrowhead forms and a newly recognized local form, making the record valuable for explicitly testing shared history against regional practice and independent innovation.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Technological resemblance is compatible with contact, shared ancestry of traditions, convergence, or independent innovation; no historical edge should be generated without chronology and contact evidence.

provenance.source: Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports / Elsevier
